chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Sayf, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, that he asked Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā (peace be upon him), who said:
"Concealment (of the intention) is more beloved to me, and do not name anything."
And that which reveals what we mentioned, that restricting oneself to the Talbiyah with Hajj and the Niyyah in Mut'ah came only as a form of Taqiyya (concealment), is what he narrated:

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةِ: The vocal recitation of 'Labbayk' during Hajj
key_terms.الْمُتْعَةِ: Mut'ah (temporary marriage or specific type of pilgrimage)

ai.seo_question: Why did the Imams prefer concealing the intention during Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) establishes that concealing the intention (Iḍmār) is superior to vocalizing it (Iʿlān), a ruling rooted in the principle of Taqiyya during periods of political tension with the Abbasid authorities. This context clarifies that while vocalizing the Talbiyah was practiced, it was often a precautionary measure rather than an intrinsic requirement, highlighting the flexibility in ritual expression based on contextual necessity.
